question: A line is tangent to a circle at point A. If a chord AB has a length of 8 cm and makes an angle of 30° with the tangent, what is the radius of the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius of a circle is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, making a 90° angle.

The angle between the radius and the given chord is 90° − 30° = 60°.

The triangle formed by the center of the circle and the chord consists of two equal radii, making it an isosceles triangle.

Since the base angles of this isosceles triangle are 60°, it is an equilateral triangle with all angles being 60°.

In an equilateral triangle, all sides are equal, so the radius equals the length of the chord, which is 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

**Given:**

Length of chord AB = 8 cm

Angle between the tangent at A and the chord AB = 30°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let O be the center of the circle, and OA and OB be the radii (R).

⇒ The radius drawn to the point of tangency is always perpendicular to the tangent line.

⇒ Total Angle between radius OA and the tangent = 90°

⇒ Angle OAB = Angle between OA and tangent − Angle between chord and tangent

⇒ Angle OAB = 90° − 30° = 60°

⇒ In triangle OAB, the sides OA and OB are equal because both are radii of the same circle (OA = OB = R).

⇒ Since angles opposite to equal sides are also equal, Angle OBA = Angle OAB = 60°.

⇒ The sum of angles in a triangle is 180°, so Angle AOB = 180° − (60° + 60°) = 60°.

⇒ Since all three interior angles are exactly 60°, triangle OAB is an equilateral triangle.

⇒ In an equilateral triangle, all three sides are equal in length.

⇒ Therefore, Radius (OA) = Radius (OB) = Chord (AB) = 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is strictly equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment of the circle.

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent to a circle is always perpendicular to the radius drawn from the center of the circle to the exact point of tangency.

Equilateral Triangle Characteristics

An isosceles triangle containing any interior angle of 60° will always result in an equilateral triangle where all three sides and angles are completely equal.
